content: The schedule for the AHA 2015 conference includes a series of interviews and presentations on various medical topics, particularly focusing on cardiovascular research and clinical trials. Sunday, November 8, 2015 At 11:00 AM, Dr. Karen Alexander will discuss the impact of incomplete revascularization on angina and quality of life following PCI, based on findings from the RIVER-PCI trial. The embargo on this information will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 11:45 AM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Mihai Gheorghiade will present findings from the SOCRATES-REDUCED study, which evaluates the oral sGC stimulator vericiguat in patients with worsening chronic heart failure and reduced ejection fraction. The embargo will lift on Sunday, November 8, 2015, at 4:13 PM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Henning Bundgaard will present the BEAT-HF trial, a first-in-human randomized study of a β3-adrenoceptor agonist in chronic heart failure. The embargo will lift on Wednesday, November 11, 2015, at 10:57 AM. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Margaret Redfield will discuss the NEAT-HFpEF trial, which examines the effects of nitrates on activity tolerance in heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction. The embargo will lift on Sunday, November 8, 2015, at 4:04 PM. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Michael Ong will present the BETTER-HF study, which evaluates remote patient management after hospital discharge for heart failure patients. The embargo will lift on Sunday, November 8, 2015, at 4:22 PM. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Bonnie Spring will discuss a clinical trial comparing simultaneous versus sequential changes in diet and physical activity using a mobile health intervention. The embargo will lift on Monday, November 9, 2015, at 11:13 AM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Iftikhar Kullo will present findings from the MI-GENES study, which investigates the impact of disclosing genomic risk for coronary heart disease on LDL cholesterol levels. The embargo will lift on Monday, November 9, 2015, at 11:22 AM. Monday, November 9, 2015 At 9:00 AM, Dr. Noel Bairey-Merz will discuss a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of ranolazine in coronary microvascular dysfunction, focusing on its effects on angina and myocardial ischemia. The embargo will lift on Wednesday, November 11, 2015, at 11:45 AM. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Robert Yeh will present an analysis of the DAPT study, which explores individualized treatment durations for dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. The embargo will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 11:30 AM. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Myeong-ki Hong will discuss the clinical outcomes of intravascular ultrasound-guided implantation of everolimus-eluting stents in long coronary lesions. The embargo will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 11:00 AM. At 11:30 AM, Drs. Geeta Gulati, Siri Heck, and Torbjørn Omland will present the PRADA trial, a randomized, placebo-controlled study on preventing cardiac dysfunction during adjuvant breast cancer therapy. The embargo will lift on Wednesday, November 11, 2015, at 11:09 AM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Basil Lewis will provide a wrap-up of AHA 2015 in Hebrew. At 12:30 PM, Dr. Douglas Mann will present one-year follow-up results from the AUGMENT-HF trial, which evaluates left ventricular augmentation with Algisyl-LVR in heart failure treatment. The embargo will lift on Wednesday, November 11, 2015, at 10:45 AM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Valentin Fuster will discuss the impact of a comprehensive lifestyle peer-group-based intervention on cardiovascular risk factors in a randomized controlled trial. The embargo will lift on Monday, November 9, 2015, at 11:04 AM. At 1:30 PM, Drs. Justin Ezekowitz and Robert Welsh will present the PROACT-4 study, which focuses on providing rapid out-of-hospital acute cardiovascular treatment. The embargo will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 10:45 AM. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Mark Eisenberg will discuss a randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of varenicline for smoking cessation in patients hospitalized with acute coronary syndrome. The embargo will lift on Monday, November 9, 2015, at 10:55 AM. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Lars Wallentin will provide a Scandinavian perspective on the AHA 2015 wrap-up. Tuesday, November 10, 2015 At 10:00 AM, Dr. The embargo will lift on Monday, November 9, 2015, at 2:05 PM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Marc Bonaca will discuss the long-term tolerability of ticagrelor in the PEGASUS-TIMI 54 trial. The embargo will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 11:15 AM. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Freek Verheugt will provide a wrap-up of AHA 2015 from a Dutch perspective. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Renato Lopes will provide a Portuguese-language wrap-up of AHA 2015. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Myeong-ki Hong will again discuss the clinical outcomes of intravascular ultrasound-guided implantation of everolimus-eluting stents in long coronary lesions. The embargo will lift on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, at 11:00 AM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Kenneth Margulies will present a randomized trial of liraglutide for high-risk heart failure patients with reduced ejection fraction. The embargo will lift on Sunday, November 8, 2015, at 3:55 PM. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Kevin Fitzgerald will discuss ALN-PCSsc, an RNAi investigational agent targeting PCSK9, with potential for quarterly or bi-annual dosing. The embargo will lift on Wednesday, November 11, 2015, at 11:57 AM. At 4:45 PM, Prof. Dr. Sigmund Silber will provide a German-language wrap-up of AHA 2015. Wednesday, November 11, 2015 At 9:30 AM, Prof. Harvey White will provide a wrap-up of AHA 2015 from a Pacific Rim perspective. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Hisao Ogawa will provide a Japanese-language wrap-up of AHA 2015. This detailed schedule outlines the key presentations and interviews, along with their respective embargo times, ensuring the timely dissemination of critical medical research findings.
